data.name: Mustashar
data.gender_notes: Mustashar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root sh-r-a, meaning to observe, watch, or supervise. In Islamic tradition, Mustashar is a name for someone who is steadfast and watchful, observing Allah's commands and following His guidance. The name Mustashar carries the meaning “Observer, Watcher” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mustashar usually hope their child will grow to embody observer, watcher and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing vigilance and dedication to Allah's path.
data.etymology: Mustashar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Observer, Watcher.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mustashar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah. Mustashar ibn Abd al-Jabbar served as the governor of Damascus during the early Abbasid Caliphate period, around 750 AD. He was known for his administration skills and his ability to maintain order and security in Damascus.

Al-Baladhuri's Ansab al-Ashraf. Mustashar ibn Abd al-Aziz was a prominent military leader during the Umayyad Caliphate, serving under Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. He was known for his bravery and skill in battle, and played a significant role in the victory against the Byzantines in the Battle of Marj al-Saffar in 739 AD.
